correctness.rationale: For p≥5, r in [2,p), n=p+r, Newton identities identify the 1..4 power-sum ideal with e1..e4; freeness over symmetric polynomial invariants makes this a regular sequence of degree 1·2·3·4=24. Vandermonde Jacobian rank equals number of distinct coordinates capped at 4; a singular projective zero has <=3 values. First s nonzero power sums and invertible Vandermonde imply multiplicities of each distinct nonzero value are divisible by p, forcing exactly p equal nonzero entries and r zeros; hence binom(n,p) singular support points. The finite singular locus and dimension n−5≥2, plus CI Cohen–Macaulay, give normality and geometric integrality via connectedness. In a chart at an indicator point, two independent linear initial forms and two quadratic forms U,V form a regular initial sequence, with restricted Gram determinants p−1 and r both nonzero; associated graded is k[u,v]/(q_{p−2}(u),q_{r−1}(v)), Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity 4, and r=2,3,≥4 produce nonreduced, reduced reducible and integral normal regimes. Independently exhaustive F5 projective points for n7 and n8 recovered exactly 21 and 56 predicted indicator singular points; Gram determinants checked across p=5,7. Computation corroborates but not replaces proof over algebraic closures.
